The breakdown of the [Treaty of Amiens](/wiki/Treaty_of_Amiens "Treaty of Amiens") led to the [War of the Third Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_Third_Coalition "War of the Third Coalition") by 1805. Napoleon shattered the coalition with a decisive victory at the [Battle of Austerlitz](/wiki/Battle_of_Austerlitz "Battle of Austerlitz"), which led to the [dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire](/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Holy_Roman_Empire "Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire"). In the [War of the Fourth Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_Fourth_Coalition "War of the Fourth Coalition"), Napoleon defeated [Prussia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Prussia "Kingdom of Prussia") at the [Battle of Jena–Auerstedt](/wiki/Battle_of_Jena%E2%80%93Auerstedt "Battle of Jena–Auerstedt") in 1806, marched his *[Grande Armée](/wiki/Grande_Arm%C3%A9e "Grande Armée")* into Eastern Europe, and defeated the [Russians](/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire") in 1807 at the [Battle of Friedland](/wiki/Battle_of_Friedland "Battle of Friedland"). Seeking to extend his [trade embargo against Britain](/wiki/Continental_System "Continental System"), Napoleon invaded the [Iberian Peninsula](/wiki/Iberian_Peninsula "Iberian Peninsula") and installed his brother [Joseph](/wiki/Joseph_Bonaparte "Joseph Bonaparte") as [King of Spain](/wiki/King_of_Spain "King of Spain") in 1808, provoking the [Peninsular War](/wiki/Peninsular_War "Peninsular War"). In 1809, the Austrians again challenged France in the [War of the Fifth Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_Fifth_Coalition "War of the Fifth Coalition"), in which Napoleon solidified his grip over Europe after winning the [Battle of Wagram](/wiki/Battle_of_Wagram "Battle of Wagram"). In the summer of 1812, he launched [an invasion of Russia](/wiki/French_invasion_of_Russia "French invasion of Russia"). Brad Stevens :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
Born and raised in [Zionsville, Indiana](/wiki/Zionsville,_Indiana "Zionsville, Indiana"), Stevens starred on the [Zionsville Community High School](/wiki/Zionsville_Community_High_School "Zionsville Community High School") basketball team, setting four school records. After high school, he attended [DePauw University](/wiki/DePauw_University "DePauw University"), where he played basketball and earned a degree in [economics](/wiki/Economics "Economics"). Stevens made the all-conference team multiple times and was a three-time [Academic All-America](/wiki/Academic_All-America "Academic All-America") nominee. He transitioned into coaching after quitting his job at [Eli Lilly and Company](/wiki/Eli_Lilly_and_Company "Eli Lilly and Company"), joining the [basketball](/wiki/Butler_Bulldogs_men%27s_basketball "Butler Bulldogs men's basketball") program at [Butler University](/wiki/Butler_University "Butler University") as a volunteer prior to the 2000–01 season. Stevens was promoted to a full-time assistant coach the following season. After five seasons in the role, he assumed the position of head coach on April 4, 2007, after [Todd Lickliter](/wiki/Todd_Lickliter "Todd Lickliter") left to coach the [Iowa Hawkeyes](/wiki/Iowa_Hawkeyes "Iowa Hawkeyes"). In his first year, Stevens led Butler to 30 wins, becoming the third-youngest head coach in [NCAA Division I](/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") history to have a 30-win season.

In 2010, his third year as head coach, Stevens broke the NCAA record for most wins in a coach's first three years, exceeding the previous record by eight wins. In the NCAA tournament, Stevens coached Butler to the first [Final Four](/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men%27s_basketball_tournament#Final_Four "2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") in school history, while also becoming the second-youngest head coach to make an NCAA national championship game, losing 61–59 to [Duke](/wiki/2009%E2%80%931

The Netherlands play most of their matches at [Johan Cruyff Arena](/wiki/Johan_Cruyff_Arena "Johan Cruyff Arena").

The Netherlands national team does not have a national stadium but plays mostly at the [Johan Cruyff Arena](/wiki/Johan_Cruyff_Arena "Johan Cruyff Arena") in [Amsterdam](/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"). It played host to its first competitive Netherlands international match back in 1997, a [1998 World Cup qualification](/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(UEFA) "1998 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)") match against [San Marino](/wiki/San_Marino_national_football_team "San Marino national football team") which the Netherlands won 4–0,[[91]](#cite_note-92) after hosting a friendly match between The Netherlands and Brazil in 1996, which ended in a 2-2 draw.[[92]](#cite_note-93) The stadium was formally called the Amsterdam Arena until 2018 when it was renamed in memory of Johan Cruyff.[[93]](#cite_note-johan-cruijff-arena-1-94)

Over the last few years, [De Kuip](/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam") has hosted matches regularly and historically very often. Occasionally, matches take place at [Philips Stadion](/wiki/Philips_Stadion "Philips Stadion") in [Eindhoven](/wiki/Eindhoven "Eindhoven") and also sometimes at the [De Grolsch Veste](/wiki/De_Grolsch_Veste "De Grolsch Veste") in [Enschede](/wiki/Enschede "Enschede").[[94]](#cite_note-stadiums-95)

Some 77% of American college students attend public institutions[[471]](#cite_note-494) such as the [University of Virginia](/wiki/University_of_Virginia "University of Virginia"), founded by [Thomas Jefferson](/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") in 1819.

American primary and secondary education, known in the U.S. as [K–12](/wiki/K%E2%80%9312_education_in_the_United_States "K–12 education in the United States") ("kindergarten through 12th grade"), is decentralized. School systems are operated by state, territorial, and sometimes municipal governments and regulated by the [U.S. Department of Education](/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education "United States Department of Education"). In general, children are required to attend school or [an approved homeschool](/wiki/Homeschooling_in_the_United_States "Homeschooling in the United States") from the age of five or six ([kindergarten](/wiki/Kindergarten "Kindergarten") or [first grade](/wiki/First_grade "First grade")) until they are 18 years old. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Interior_of_Taj%2C_Agra_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Interior_of_Taj%2C_Agra_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Interior_of_Taj,_Agra_(cropped).jpg)

A *[jali](/wiki/Jali "Jali")* screen surrounding the cenotaphs

The main inner chamber is an octagon with 7.3-metre (24 ft) sides, with the design allowing for entry from each face with the main door facing the garden to the south. Two tiers of eight *pishtaq* arches are located along the walls, similar to the exterior.[[35]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKhatri2012128-35) The four central upper arches form balconies or viewing areas, and each balcony's exterior window has an intricate *jali*. The inner wall is open along the axes where *jali* screens are fitted which transmit light from the exterior to the interior of the main chamber.[[36]](#cite_note-Arch3-36) Except the south side, other three sides consist of an open elongated room flanked by two square cells covered with decorated ceilings set on the platform. The central room has arched openings on three sides fitted with *jalis* filled with panes of glass and a small rectangular window cut into the central *jali*.[[36]](#cite_note-Arch3-36) The square cells which are reached through separate doors were probably originally used for visitors and Qur'an reciters as a place to rest. Staircases lead from the ground floor to the roof level, where there are corridors between the central hall and the two corner rooms in the south with a system of ventilation shafts.[[24]](#cite_note-Arch2-24)

From 1905 to 1908, the [Long Island Rail Road](/wiki/Long_Island_Rail_Road "Long Island Rail Road") in Queens became electrified. Transportation to and from [Manhattan](/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), previously by ferry or via bridges in Brooklyn, opened up with the [Queensboro Bridge](/wiki/Queensboro_Bridge "Queensboro Bridge") finished in 1909, and with railway tunnels under the [East River](/wiki/East_River "East River") in 1910. From 1915 onward, much of Queens was connected to the [New York City Subway](/wiki/New_York_City_Subway "New York City Subway") system.[[28]](#cite_note-Seyfried-Peterson-28)[[56]](#cite_note-Seyfried_2004-56) With the 1915 construction of the [Steinway Tunnel](/wiki/Steinway_Tunnel "Steinway Tunnel") carrying the [IRT Flushing Line](/wiki/IRT_Flushing_Line "IRT Flushing Line") between Queens and Manhattan, and the robust expansion of the use of the [automobile](/wiki/Automobile "Automobile"), the population of Queens more than doubled in the 1920s, from 469,042 in 1920 to 1,079,129 in 1930.[[57]](#cite_note-Gibson_1998_Jun-57)

In later years, Queens was the site of the [1939 New York World's Fair](/wiki/1939_New_York_World%27s_Fair "1939 New York World's Fair") and the [1964 New York World's Fair](/wiki/1964_New_York_World%27s_Fair "1964 New York World's Fair").[[58]](#cite_note-58) [LaGuardia Airport](/wiki/LaGuardia_Airport "LaGuardia Airport"), established on a site in northern Queens that had been a seaplane base, opened in 1939, named for mayor [Fiorello La Guardia](/wiki/Fiorello_La_Guardia "Fiorello La Guardia"), who pushed for the development of a modern airport in New York City.[[59]](#cite_note-59) Idlewild Airport, in southern Queens, opened in 1948 on the site of a former golf course and was renamed [John F. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Eisenhower_House_1.jpg/330px-Eisenhower_House_1.jpg)](/wiki/File:Eisenhower_House_1.jpg)

The Eisenhower family home in Abilene, Kansas

Eisenhower was born David Dwight Eisenhower in [Denison, Texas](/wiki/Denison,_Texas "Denison, Texas"), on October 14, 1890, the third of seven sons born to Ida and David.[[8]](#cite_note-9) His mother soon reversed his two forenames after his birth to avoid the confusion of having two Davids in the family.[[9]](#cite_note-A18-10) He was named Dwight after the evangelist [Dwight L. Moody](/wiki/Dwight_L._Moody "Dwight L. Moody").[[10]](#cite_note-11) All of the boys were nicknamed "Ike", such as "Big Ike" ([Edgar](/wiki/Edgar_N._Eisenhower "Edgar N. Eisenhower")) and "Little Ike" (Dwight); the nickname was intended as an abbreviation of their last name.[[11]](#cite_note-12) By World War II, only Dwight was still called "Ike".[[4]](#cite_note-barnett19421109-5)

In 1892, the family moved to [Abilene, Kansas](/wiki/Abilene,_Kansas "Abilene, Kansas"), which Eisenhower considered his hometown.[[4]](#cite_note-barnett19421109-5) As a child, he was involved in an accident that cost his younger brother [Earl](/wiki/Earl_D._Eisenhower "Earl D. Eisenhower") an eye, for which he was remorseful for the remainder of his life.[[12]](#cite_note-13) Eisenhower developed a keen and enduring interest in exploring the outdoors. He learned about hunting and fishing, cooking, and card playing from a man named Bob Davis who camped on the [Smoky Hill River](/wiki/Smoky_Hill_River "Smoky Hill River").[[13]](#cite_note-ease-14)[[14]](#cite_note-15)[[15]](#cite_note-16) While his mother was against war, it was her collection of history books that first sparked Eisenhower's interest in military history; he became a voracious reader on the subject. Other favorite subjects early in his education were arithmetic and spelling.[[16]]

[![Cameron in September 1986](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/James_Cameron.jpg/250px-James_Cameron.jpg)](/wiki/File:James_Cameron.jpg)

Cameron, September 1986

Cameron's directing career began in 1978.[[17]](#cite_note-17) After borrowing money from a consortium of dentists, he learned to direct, write and produce his first short film, *[Xenogenesis](/wiki/Xenogenesis_(film) "Xenogenesis (film)")* (1978), with a friend.[[18]](#cite_note-18) Learning as he went, Cameron said he felt like a doctor doing his first surgical procedure.[[15]](#cite_note-Syd_Field-15) He then served as a production assistant for *[Rock 'n' Roll High School](/wiki/Rock_%27n%27_Roll_High_School "Rock 'n' Roll High School")* (1979). While educating himself about filmmaking techniques, Cameron started a job as a miniature [model maker](/wiki/Model_maker "Model maker") at [Roger Corman](/wiki/Roger_Corman "Roger Corman") Studios.[[14]](#cite_note-filmmakers.com-14)[[19]](#cite_note-19) He was soon employed as an art director for the science-fiction film *[Battle Beyond the Stars](/wiki/Battle_Beyond_the_Stars "Battle Beyond the Stars")* (1980). He carried out the special effects for [John Carpenter](/wiki/John_Carpenter "John Carpenter")'s *[Escape from New York](/wiki/Escape_from_New_York "Escape from New York")* (1981), served as production designer for *[Galaxy of Terror](/wiki/Galaxy_of_Terror "Galaxy of Terror")* (1981), and consulted on the design for *[Android](/wiki/Android_(film) "Android (film)")* (1982).

Cameron was hired as the visual effects director for the sequel to *[Piranha](/wiki/Piranha_(1978_film) "Piranha (1978 film)")* (1978), titled *[Piranha II: The Spawning](/wiki/Piranha_II:_The_Spawning "Piranha II: The Spawning")* in 1982. Stefani performing "Hollaback Girl" in 2007 at [The Sweet Escape Tour](/wiki/The_Sweet_Escape_Tour "The Sweet Escape Tour")

As part of [Gwen Stefani](/wiki/Gwen_Stefani "Gwen Stefani")'s vision of creating "a silly [dance](/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music") record",[[2]](#cite_note-2) she had worked with [the Neptunes](/wiki/The_Neptunes "The Neptunes") ([Pharrell](/wiki/Pharrell_Williams "Pharrell Williams") and [Chad Hugo](/wiki/Chad_Hugo "Chad Hugo")) during the early stages of writing songs for her debut solo album *[Love. Angel. Music. Baby.](/wiki/Love._Angel._Music._Baby. "Love. Angel. Music. Baby.")*. However, a case of [writer's block](/wiki/Writer%27s_block "Writer's block") resulted in reportedly uninspired collaborations.[[1]](#cite_note-making-1) As the album neared completion, Stefani regained her confidence and booked another session with the Neptunes. Stefani flew to New York City to meet up with Pharrell, and after finishing two songs within a week, Stefani ended the session early and prepared to return home. A few minutes later, Pharrell called her back into the studio to write another song. Stefani said, "I was tired. I wanted to go home, but he was like, 'Don't leave yet.'"[[3]](#cite_note-attitude-3) When she returned to the studio, Pharrell began to play Stefani his first solo album, the then-unreleased *[In My Mind](/wiki/In_My_Mind_(Pharrell_Williams_album) "In My Mind (Pharrell Williams album)")*, and she became envious.[[1]](#cite_note-making-1) Excited by his material, she decided to write another song with Pharrell, despite her opinion that the album already contained far too many tracks.[[3]](#cite_note-attitude-3)
